title: Lord Cobham (Ostend) to Walsingham, 20-22 March 1587/8, BL Harley MS 287 ff. 70-72 (DECODE R8482-R8487)

steps.what: Fetched the seven page images and the key record R8497 from DECODE with the session cookie.
Checked CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4, March 1588 sections, for these letters.
Compared the Bodley 1590 key R8497 in the same volume.
Cipher runs beside clear words read as 'commaunded to attend', 'that bearer hath', 'instructions', 'under colour thereof', 'any money', fixing most letters.
Read the runs of ff. 70r-72v word by word from context; long runs on f. 70v and 71v read in sense (preparations, eleven companies of footmen, subject to interception).
The cobham1588 session found the same letter values in the contemporary glosses of f. 89 (R8493).

Second pass on full-resolution half-line crops: remaining runs of f. 70r (canal Ghent-Eecloo-Sluys, garrison, victuals), names Pigot and Barney on f. 72r, the last lines of f. 71r; nomenclator signs 15 (Parma) and square (the States) identified from context.
CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4 confirms Captain Barney a prisoner at Ostend and the request for 2 or 3 pinnaces, 22 March 1588.

outcome.notes: Every run of ff. 70r-72v read; code 42, .7. and one surname uncertain. f. 11 (R8477), a different code of about eight groups, not read.

prior.where: DECODE lists the records as partially/non-decrypted; no decipherment on the leaves; CSP Foreign 1588 calendars other Cobham letters but not these

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
